judge.reasoning:
Overall (8): The report is genuinely useful for site selection. It progresses logically from regional overview → age concentration → education/self-employment → income/spending power → a synthesized shortlist with concrete ZIP recommendations (97214, 97202, flagged 97209 and 97212). The final recommendation is specific and actionable, correctly focusing on inner-eastside/central Portland ZIPs that match the "trendy, walkable arts district" brief.

Section relevance (9): Every section maps tightly to the ideal customer (music enthusiasts 20-45, creatives, remote workers, students). Age concentration, self-employment (a smart proxy for the remote-worker/"lingerer" and local-artist supply), education, and discretionary income are all directly on-point. No filler sections. Minor gap: nothing on rent/commercial-lease cost, foot traffic proximity to venues, or renter share — all central to the brief's location and $4-6k lease constraints — so it stops just short of full location due diligence.

Narrative quality (8): Narratives are specific, tie numbers to business decisions (premium vs. value product mix by ZIP, evening listening-party programming where 30s cohort peaks, pop-ups for price-sensitive outer-east), and avoid generic filler. However there are internal inconsistencies that erode accuracy: the summary claims Portland median age 39.7 and Multnomah 38.7 while Section 1 calls Multnomah "youngest median age (38.7)" then also says "38.72" — fine — but Section 2 titles a chart "Aged 20-45" while summing 20s+30s+40s (which is 20-49), and Section 5's viz title literally says "Aged 20-49" then subtitle calls it the 20-45 proxy. The 20-45 band is repeatedly approximated by 20-49, an overstatement the narrative doesn't flag. Also 97227's "32.3% in 30s" and similar figures are cited confidently but the age proxy inflation is a real accuracy issue.

Data plausibility (7): Most values are plausible for close-in Portland — median incomes $85k-$103k, college attainment 50%+, Pearl District density ~8,357/sq mi, self-employment 11-20%. But several figures are aggressive: 97239 at 75.4% bachelor's+graduate and 44.3% of households earning $150k+ in 97212 are on the high side though not impossible for affluent Portland pockets. More concerning are cross-section inconsistencies: 97209's "20s-40s" share is 67.9% in Section 2/5 but the summary/opportunity chart lists 97214 x-value 46.3 (20s-30s) vs Section 5's 63.0% (20s-40s) — different denominators used without clear labeling. Washington County population shown as 87,096 and Clackamas 67,709 are implausibly low for whole counties (Washington County is ~600k), suggesting these are partial/urban-area subsets — a labeling problem that could mislead. That drags plausibility down.

Visualization appropriateness (6): Bubble charts are well-used for the multi-dimensional opportunity/education/income analyses — appropriate and information-dense. Bar charts for county comparisons and age-bracket breakdowns fit categorical data. However, several charts are mis-typed: Section 2 viz-1, Section 4 viz-1, and Section 5 viz-1 are labeled "histogram" but plot a per-ZIP value (share aged 20-45, share $150k+) — some with x-axis "ZIP code" and y-axis "%", which is actually a bar chart, not a histogram (a histogram bins a distribution). Section 4/5 histograms with "Number of ZIP codes" on y are legitimate histograms, so usage is inconsistent. The Section 3 violin plot for only 21 ZIP points is weak — a violin/KDE over 21 discrete points is a stretch; a strip/box plot would be more honest. These type mismatches are exactly the kind of thing the rubric penalizes.

Tool selection (9): Metric selection is excellent and well-reasoned for this business: age distribution, education, self-employment (creative/remote-worker proxy), household income distribution ($150k+ share for discretionary spend), labor force participation, and population density. Self-employment as a proxy for both weekday lingerers and local-artist supply is a genuinely insightful choice. Only missing metrics that would matter: renter share/housing tenure (home_ownership_rate is null), and any commercial-rent or foot-traffic data relevant to the lease budget and walkability brief.
